Requirement Statement: The firmware shall target the STM32-NUCLEO-G070RB development board.

Acceptance Criteria: The firmware is built for and runs on the STM32-NUCLEO-G070RB development board.

Acceptance Criteria: Temperature and humidity readings are acquired from the DHT22 using PB4.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall interface with an MPU6050 3-axis accelerometer and gyroscope over I2C on PB8 (SCL) and PB9 (SDA), sharing the bus with the OLED.

Postconditions / Expected Behavior: The above-limit value is marked with "!".

Postconditions / Expected Behavior: X, Y, and Z acceleration values in g are available.

Parameters / Constraints: Calibration duration: 1 s; calibrated outputs: X = 0 g, Y = 0 g, Z = 1 g.

Postconditions / Expected Behavior: The X/Y/Z readings are zeroed to the stated values.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall map X acceleration to lateral cornering, Y acceleration to longitudinal acceleration/braking, and Z acceleration to vertical bumps.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall detect an event when its associated axis changes by at least the configured threshold within 100 ms.

Parameters / Constraints: Sudden-change window: 100 ms.
Preconditions: MPU6050 acceleration readings are available.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: A qualifying change is detected as an event.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall detect and identify Unseen SpeedBreaker when Z changes by at least 0.30 g, Wide Turn when X changes by at least 0.25 g, Speeding when Y changes positively by at least 0.25 g, and Sudden Braking when Y changes negatively by at least 0.25 g.
Source Text / Evidence: Unseen SpeedBreaker Z changes by 0.30 g or more; Wide Turn X changes by 0.25 g or more; Speeding Y changes by +0.25 g or more (indicates harsh acceleration, not actual speed); Sudden Braking Y changes by -0.25 g or more (negative direction) | Z (Unseen SpeedBreaker) 0.30 g Quick tap or lift-and-drop 0.4-0.5 g | X (Wide Turn) 0.25 g Quick flick left or right 0.4-0.5 g | +Y (Speeding) +0.25 g Quick push forward 0.4-0.5 g | -Y (Sudden Braking) -0.25 g Quick pull backward 0.4-0.5 g
Acceptance Criteria: Changes meeting the configured demo thresholds identify: Unseen SpeedBreaker at Z >= 0.30 g; Wide Turn at X >= 0.25 g; Speeding at positive Y >= 0.25 g; Sudden Braking at negative Y >= 0.25 g in magnitude. In-vehicle values are configurable as Z 0.4-0.5 g, X 0.4-0.5 g, +Y 0.4-0.5 g, and -Y 0.4-0.5 g.
Parameters / Constraints: Demo thresholds: Z 0.30 g, X 0.25 g, +Y +0.25 g, -Y -0.25 g. In-vehicle thresholds: Z, X, +Y, and -Y each 0.4-0.5 g. Speeding indicates harsh acceleration, not actual speed.
Expected Value / Range: Demo: Z 0.30 g; X 0.25 g; +Y +0.25 g; -Y -0.25 g. In-vehicle: each 0.4-0.5 g.
Preconditions: MPU6050 acceleration readings are available and zeroed.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: The qualifying event type is identified.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall initialize the SH1106 display interface before its first display write, early enough for the logo to appear within 100 ms of power-up.
Source PRD Section: Acceptance Criteria for the Logo (p. 3); Hardware (p. 1)
Source Text / Evidence: The logo appears within 100 ms of power-up and stays for 2 s +/- 100 ms. | Display: 1.3" OLED (SH1106 driver), I2C
Inference Rationale: The logo cannot be written to the OLED within the stated power-up deadline unless the display interface is initialized before the first write.
Acceptance Criteria: Following power-up, the display interface is initialized before the first logo write, and the logo appears within 100 ms.
Parameters / Constraints: Display initialization must precede the first display write; logo onset deadline is 100 ms after power-up.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall coordinate access to the shared I2C bus so transactions to the MPU6050 and OLED do not overlap or corrupt one another.
Source Text / Evidence:
MPU6050 SCL         PB8 (shared with OLED)
MPU6050 SDA            PB9 (shared with OLED)
OLED SCL         PB8 (shared with MPU6050)
OLED SDA         PB9 (shared with MPU6050)
Inference Rationale: The MPU6050 and OLED use the same I2C signal lines. Uncoordinated simultaneous transactions can prevent reliable sensor acquisition or display updates, so the stated shared-bus functions cannot be relied upon without coordinated access.
Acceptance Criteria: During concurrent requests for MPU6050 and OLED operations, bus transactions do not overlap and each requested operation completes without corruption attributable to another transaction.
Parameters / Constraints: Coordinate transactions on the shared I2C bus.
Preconditions: The MPU6050 and OLED share the I2C bus.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Each device transaction is performed without overlap with another device transaction.

Requirement Statement: The firmware shall detect failed DHT22 or MPU6050 acquisitions and shall not use failed acquisition results as valid displayed measurements or inputs to event detection.
Source Text / Evidence:
Read temperature (degC) and humidity (%) from the DHT22 every 2 seconds.
Read X, Y, Z acceleration from the MPU6050 (+/-4 g range, 100 Hz) and convert to g.
When an event occurs, the message appears immediately on the OLED while Temperature and Humidity stay visible.
Inference Rationale: Failed sensor transactions can produce unusable data. Without detecting and excluding those results, firmware could display invalid measurements or generate event alerts from data that was not successfully acquired, undermining the stated monitoring and event-detection behavior.
Acceptance Criteria: When a DHT22 or MPU6050 acquisition fails, its failed result is not presented as a valid measurement and is not used to trigger an event.
Parameters / Constraints: Handle failed sensor acquisitions without treating their results as valid measurements or event-detection inputs.
Preconditions: A DHT22 or MPU6050 acquisition is attempted.
Postconditions / Expected Behavior: Failed acquisition results are excluded from measurement presentation and event detection.
Comments / Open Questions: The PRD does not specify how sensor failure should be indicated to the user or how recovery should occur.
